properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Caldwell County in western North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 830 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots. Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.  A
few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A
small culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 522 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated several period of heavy
rain have occurred between Lenoir and Patterson over the past 2-3
hours.  A stripe of 2-3 inches of rainfall has already occurred.
Another brief round of heavy rain, capable of producing another
0.5-1" of rainfall over the next 30 minutes, is currently moving
through this area.  Given saturated soils, areas of excessive
runoff are expected across the Advisory area.  Swollen small
streams may briefly reach bankfull over the next 60 minutes in
response to this runoff.  Nuisance flooding of adjacent low-lying
areas and high flows over low-water crossings are briefly
expected. Areas of greatest concern include in the Blair Fork
watershed near US 321 and along Valway Rd (NC 90), along Mill
Pond Branch near Collettsville Rd (NC 90), and Warrior Creek near
Warrior Rd and Coy Miller Rd.

- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
northern Lenoir, Cedar Rock and Patterson.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.description:

Southwestern Morgan County in southeastern Ohio...

remain vigilant into the early evening hours for
additional rises of creeks and streams.

Chesterhill, Amesville, Bartlett and Fleming.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Morgan County in southeastern Ohio...

* WHEN...Until 400 AM EDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Muskingum River at and near
McConnelsville is expected this afternoon and evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1219 PM EDT, The gauge at McConnelsville on the Muskingum
River was reading 6.1 feet and rising. The river is forecast to
crest near 7.5 feet this evening. Due to the recent dam
replacement, the official flood stage is no longer representative
of known impacts. Flooding of areas away from the gauge can be
expected at lower stages. At stages of 7.5 feet, sections of
Route 669 above Malta and other roads along the river being to
flood. In addition, low-lying areas adjacent to the river,
including recreational boat ramps, will also experience flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
McConnelsville, Malta, Stockport and Eagleport.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Wilmington has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers...

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/iln.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Hocking River at Enterprise.

* WHEN...From this evening to late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Water spills into Kachemacher Park in Logan
and onto low-lying roads near Haydenville Road at some locations
along the river.  Also, water will be across State Route 93 just
south of Logan.  Lowland flooding also occurs in Rockbridge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:00 PM EDT Tuesday the stage was 8.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
evening to a crest of 14.0 feet just after midnight tonight. It
will then fall below flood stage tomorrow evening.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
